claims: C1 the training-manual analogy establishes that the manual itself should not be disclosed unless policy explicitly allows it
C2 the assistant can share its identity and capabilities
C3 the assistant keeps underlying system or developer prompts private by default

concepts.name: assistant_identity_capabilities
concepts.gloss: the assistant's identity and capabilities, which the analogy says it can share
concepts.inference: the source text says the assistant can share its identity and capabilities, so a class of such shareable content is presupposed

concepts.name: underlying_prompts
concepts.gloss: the underlying system or developer prompts, which the analogy says are kept private by default

concepts.name: explicit_disclosure_policy
concepts.gloss: a policy that explicitly allows disclosure of the manual or the underlying prompts
concepts.inference: the source text conditions disclosure on 'policy explicitly allows it', so a class of such policies is presupposed

concepts.name: private_by_default_content
concepts.gloss: content that is the manual itself or the underlying prompts, which is private by default
concepts.inference: the analogy equates the manual with the underlying prompts for the purpose of the default-privacy claim

concepts.name: assistant_definition
concepts.gloss: the assistant as the Model Spec defines it
concepts.inference: the source text speaks of 'the assistant' without defining it; the shared-name contract supplies the meaning

concepts.name: root_authority
concepts.gloss: R carries the root level of instruction authority (highest; not overridable by system, developer or user instructions)
concepts.inference: the NEEDS contract assigns this meaning; this node's text does not define it

ontology.gloss: the underlying system or developer prompts are private by default
